metadata.source_title: Genetics and Analysis of Quantitative Traits

blocks.content: The likelihood functions developed above can be easily modified to accommodate complex segregation analysis of dichotomous (binary) characters, such as the presence/absence of a disease (e.g., Elston and Rao 1978). Define the penetrance

$\psi_{g}$ of a genotype $g$ as the probability that a random individual of that genotype displays the trait. Coding the character as $$ y=\left\{\begin{array}{l l}{0}&{\mathrm{d o e s~n o t~d i s p l a y~t h e~t r a i t}}\\ {1}&{\mathrm{d i s p l a y s~t h e~t r a i t}}\end{array}\right. $$ gives the likelihood function for an individual with genotype g as $$ \ell(y\mid g)=(\psi_{g})^{y}\left(1-\psi_{g}\right)^{1-y}=\left\{\begin{matrix}1-\psi_{g}&\text{for}y=0\\ \psi_{g}&\text{for}y=1\end{matrix}\right. $$

More generally, if the character has $n$ discrete states, and $\psi_{k,g}$ is the probability that an individual of genotype $g$ has character state $k$, the likelihood function becomes $$ \ell(\mathbf{\textit{y}}|\mathbf{\textit{g}})=\prod_{k=1}^{n}\left(\psi_{k,g}\right)^{\delta(\mathbf{\textit{y}},k)}\qquad\mathrm{w h e r e}\qquad\delta(\mathbf{\textit{y}},k)=\left\{\begin{array}{l l}{1}&{\mathrm{i f~}\mathbf{\textit{y}}=k}\\ {0}&{\mathrm{o t h e r w i s e}}\end{array}\right. $$
Thus, our treatment below of dichotomous characters easily extends to polychotomous traits.
